newsitem.title: FINLAND: Valmet CEO sees gradual forestry recovery.
newsitem.headline: Valmet CEO sees gradual forestry recovery.

text.p: The world's leading paper machine maker Valmet Oy expects a recovery of European forest product markets from the current slowdown to be gradual, Valmet President and CEO Matti Sundberg said on Tuesday.

"I would guess pulp prices and then prices also in different paper grades will strengthen gradually, but I don't see any rapid development" Sundberg told a news conference, when asked to comment on the outlook for the European forest industry.
Sundberg expected more consolidation in the forest industry as Finnish and Swedish producers start expanding operations outside Europe.
"After ten years, there will probably be no more than about 20 significant forest industry producers in the world," he said.
Valmet said in its January-August interim report that there was not yet any certainty of any widespread price increases in pulp prices which normally lead the way for paper prices.
Sundberg said the outlook for paper machine demand was steady and he did not expect any boom.

Valmet said in its interim report that "the level of interest in new investments has continued (to be) low in North America and Europe, whereas investment activity has remained at a good level in Asia".

"The region's largest paper producer Japan experienced strong investment demand during the early part of the year when, after a few quiet years, Japanese companies ordered several new paper machines," it said.
